LearningGoals: Comprehend that probabilities from simulations may differ from expected probabilities.
Use data to critique (orally and in writing) mathematical claims based on a model in different cases.
SourceAuthority: Local Kendall Hunt archival teacher/student pages; AccessIM v360 excluded

CoreMathWorkedExample.Question: A fair coin produces 7 heads in 10 simulated flips. Is this proof the chance of heads is 70%?
Steps: Observed proportion7/10=.7 differs from fair theoretical .5
10 trials are too few for conclusive bias.
CoreMathWorkedExample.Answer: No; random variation can explain it.

GradingRubric: teacher verifies diagrams, graphs, card work and explanation
